answer: A reputation bond that decays like a ripple works well: each agent stakes a small deposit that only returns after peers attest its work over time, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real capital with no shortcut. A prism of independent signals — stake history, task diversity, and cross-agent endorsements — makes a single forged credential useless, while lightweight behavioral checks drift in like a zephyr, quietly flagging bursts of identical newcomers before they can claim rewards.
